text:
jana (eng): hey team — question about a dental implant charge. had implant placement on 2026-06-10 at Riverbend Dental. Provider says they billed CPT 42670 but my EOB says 'not covered - cosmetic' and denied. I'm on Premier Plus plan. claim# 3344556677. member id last4 2143. any idea how to proceed?

eli (People Ops): ugh. implants are often excluded under standard dental unless you bought the implant rider. do you recall if you had an add-on for implants when you enrolled?

jana (eng): i don't think so — i only signed up during OE and back then i picked Premier Plus default. my benefits summary pdf doesn't mention implants explicitly.

marta (Benefits): quick triage: two possibilities — 1) implants are excluded under dental benefits and carrier will deny as cosmetic, or 2) provider submitted under a dental code but carrier expects a medical claim (if it was done in a hospital or with IV sedation) and routed to medical policy which may have a different coverage rule. can you share the EOB line and provider billing name?

jana (eng): EOB line reads: "Procedure 42670 — Denied: Not a covered dental benefit (cosmetic). Allowed $0.00, Patient responsibility $1,200." Provider billed as "Riverbend Oral Surgery PC" and Tax ID 98-7654321.

dave (Billing): if the provider performed this in an oral surgery office and used a dental ledger, carrier usually adjudicates under dental plan. if it was billed to medical carrier (UB04), we might have a different shot. also check for preauthorization requirement — some carriers require preauth or narrative justification for implants tied to functional need (e.g., trauma, congenital).

marta (Benefits): can you upload the itemized invoice, pre-op note (if any), and operative note? If there was documentation of medical necessity (trauma, pathology, or tooth loss due to disease), we can submit an appeal with clinical notes. If it's purely elective (cosmetic), most plans exclude.

jana (eng): i have the operative note and X-ray. attaching in DM now. this was because of a fractured tooth after a bike fall — wasn't cosmetic.

eli (People Ops): ok please also sign the HIPAA release so benefits can speak to the carrier and provider on your behalf: https://benefits.example.com/claims-portal. we'll open a carrier inquiry once uploaded.

marta (Benefits): sample request we usually send to providers/carriers when arguing medical necessity: ```service_date: 2026-06-10
claim_id: 3344556677
patient_last4: 2143
procedure: 42670 (dental implant)
clinical_summary: implant placed for replacement after traumatic tooth fracture; attached: operative note, x-ray, clinical photos
request: re-adjudicate under medical necessity exception or consider payment under medical benefits if applicable
```

dave (Billing): also ask Riverbend to resubmit with supporting docs and include the place_of_service code and whether anesthesia was provided. if they billed under dental clearinghouse only, some carriers won't review medical justification until provider re-files to medical.

claims-bot: Carrier case opened: IMPL-2026-551. Typical carrier turnaround for appeals/clinical review: 15-30 business days. We'll request expedited review given traumatic etiology.

eli (People Ops): @jana if carrier denies and it's clearly a plan admin error or if the provider miscoded, Redwood policy may provide temporary assistance for out-of-pocket while appeal is pending — upload receipt and request an advance here: https://payments.example.com/advances (select "medical/dental appeal advance").

jana (eng): uploaded docs + DM'ed HIPAA release. thanks for the guidance. really appreciate the fast help.

marta (Benefits): got them. i'll draft the appeal packet and submit to the carrier, requesting reprocessing under medical necessity with attached operative note and x-ray. i'll update thread when the carrier responds.

eli (People Ops): thanks @marta. @jana we'll follow up — if carrier requires provider to refile to medical, i'll loop Riverbend billing manager in. in the meantime, hang tight. :white_check_mark:
